'''''Carex appressa''''', the '''tall sedge''', is a species of flowering plant in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Cyperaceae]].<ref name="nsw.gov.au">{{cite web |url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=carex~appressa |title=''Carex appressa'' |work=PlantNET – FloraOnline |author=K. L. Wilson |date=2011 |publisher=New South Wales Flora Online |accessdate=11 May 2016}}</ref> It is native to [[New Guinea]], Australia, New Zealand, and generally in the [[South West Pacific]].<ref>{{cite book |title=World Economic Plants: A Standard Reference |author=John H. Wiersema |author2=Blanca León |edition=illustrated |publisher=CRC Press |year=2016 |isbn=9781466576810 |page=143}}</ref> 

==Description==

''Carex appressa'' is a densely tufted, [[perennial]] sedge that forms clumps up to {{cvt|50|cm}} in diameter. Its stems grow to around {{cvt|100|cm}} in height, and are hard and solid, becoming rough towards the top of the stem. Its leaves are {{cvt|3-6|mm}} wide, are rough on the [[Leaf margin|margins]], and grow mostly out of the base of the plant. It has a brownish, spike-like [[inflorescence]] made of 20 or more spikes, growing {{cvt|5-25|cm}} long. Its flowers are numerous oval-shaped brownish spikelets that are approximately {{cvt|5|mm}} long, with both male and female flowers mixed together in the spikes. Its nut is contained in a flattened, oval-shaped, [[Glossary of botanical terms#beak|beaked]], hairless sack or [[Glossary of botanical terms#utricle|utricle]] that is {{cvt|3-3.5|mm}} long.<ref name=southwest >{{cite book |title=Plants of Western New South Wales |author=GM Cunningham |author2=Geoffrey McIver Cunningham |edition=illustrated |publisher=Csiro Publishing |year=2011 |isbn=9780643103634 |page=155}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=Flora of the South West: Bunbury, Augusta, Denmark |author=Judith Roderick Wheeler |author2=N. G. Marchant |author3=Margaret Lewington |publisher=UWA Publishing |year=2002 |isbn=9780642568144 |page=267}}</ref>
[[File:Carex appressa R.Br. (AM AK351569).jpg|center|thumb|[[Auckland Museum]] (AM AK351569)]]

==Habitat and ecology==

''Carex appressa'' occurs in swamps, watercourses, and occasionally in water.<ref name=southwest /> It also serves as a [[Larval food plants of Lepidoptera|larval food plant]] for ''Heteronympha cordace''.<ref>{{cite book |title=Butterflies: Identification and life history |author=Ross Field |edition=revised |publisher=Museum Victoria |year=2013 |isbn=9781921833328 |page=188}}</ref>
